This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice N.S.Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The insurer is in appeal challenging the award of Rs.5,90,000/- granted as compensation to the claimant.

2. The fact that an accident occurred on 28.05.2012 when the brother and son of the claimant were riding pillion when an accident occurred between the motorcycle and a Tata Ace vehicle, as a result of which, the deceased Syed Khan suffered serious injuries and ultimately succumbed to the same is not in dispute.

3. It was the defence of the insurer of the motorcycle that, the police had initially registered a case against the NC: 2024:KHC-K:6908 driver of the Tata Ace vehicle and subsequently had filed 'C'
report and on coming to know of this 'C' report, the claimants along with the police had created a false story and laid a charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.
So, it was therefore, contended that there was no liability on the owner of the motorcycle as he was not negligent in any way.

4. It is settled law that, the claimant is entitled to proceed against a tort feasor of his choice and it is not necessary that he would have to array both the tort feasors in his claim petition. The claimant,
having chosen to proceed against the owner of the motorcycle in which the deceased was traveling,
was therefore entitled to maintain the claim.

Merely because, the initial complaint was against the The Iffco Tokio General vs Sarakhan And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105026293/
2 driver of the Tata Ace and subsequently a 'C' report was filed that by itself, would not lead to an inference that the filing of the charge sheet was motivated or was collusive.
